response.title: Following the Stream
response.passage: On Thursday, Ms. Wu’s class visited a narrow stream behind their school. Their assignment was to compare the water’s clarity at two marked spots, not to collect animals. Ms. Wu asked each team to release a small leaf at a starting line and time how long it took to reach a stick downstream. The leaf moved steadily toward the stick, carried by the current. At the straight upper stretch, it took eight seconds to travel the marked distance. At a shaded bend, the same distance took nineteen seconds. One student guessed that the bend’s water was moving faster because it looked darker. However, the teams repeated the test three times, and the leaf was slower at the bend each time. Ms. Wu asked them to report the timed results separately from their visual impressions. In their final notes, the students concluded that the current carried the leaf faster at the straight stretch than at the bend.

items.answer: The class used repeated measurements to compare the current at two stream locations.
distractors: The class collected animals to compare the wildlife at two stream locations.
The class judged water speed by color instead of timing a floating leaf.
The class found that the current carried the leaf faster at the shaded bend.
items.question: What is the passage mainly about?

items.answer: The leaf traveled the marked distance faster at the straight upper stretch than at the bend.
distractors: The leaf traveled the marked distance faster at the shaded bend than at the upper stretch.
The leaf traveled the marked distance in the same time at both stream locations.
The leaf reached the downstream stick only after the teams removed it from the water.
items.question: What did the teams’ timing show?

items.answer: The darker appearance alone did not show that the water was moving faster at the bend.
distractors: The repeated tests confirmed that the darker water moved faster at the bend.
The teams stopped timing because the stream became too dark to observe.
The class decided that a leaf’s color determined how quickly the water carried it.
